the gas-sensing performance of carbon nanomaterials coated with metal oxide is determined by the morphology and density (thickness) of the metal oxide layer.

the sensing mechanism of SnO2-CNT and SnO2-RGO composites can be understood in terms of a general model that considers the influence of the SnO2 coating thickness and the morphology of carbon nanostructures, and that the sensing mechanism is not limited to the specific target gas (i.e., NO2) investigated in this work.
the sensing properties of carbon-based materials can be significantly enhanced by coating with SnO2, and that this effect depends on the SnO2 morphology.

the synthesis and characterization of tin dioxide-carbon heterojunctions, and the investigation of their gas-sensing behavior.
the synthesis and characterization of SnO2-coated carbon nanotubes and reduced graphene oxide and their application as sensing materials.
the synthesis and characterization of SnO2-CNT and SnO2-RGO heterostructures and the investigation of their sensing behavior towards NO2 gas.

the sensing mechanism of SnO2/RuOx heterostructures can be described as a two-step process.
